provenance.reasoning: 'fast' has no number, percentile, or measurement point; two people can disagree about whether it was met.
provenance.source_quote: The login flow must be fast

findings.suggested_rewrite: p95 login completes in under 2 seconds, measured from the IdP redirect to app landing.

provenance.reasoning: Reads precise but is not: no percentile, no load condition, no measurement point. 'Under a second' at p50 idle and at p99 peak are different requirements.
provenance.source_quote: Token refresh must complete in under a second

findings.suggested_rewrite: Token refresh completes in under 1 second at p95 under peak sign-in load, measured at the gateway.

provenance.reasoning: 'a large number' is not a capacity target; it cannot size infrastructure or a load test.
provenance.source_quote: The system must support a large number of concurrent sessions during peak sign-in

findings.suggested_rewrite: Support 12,000 concurrent sessions at peak sign-in (Monday 09:00 UTC), with headroom to 2x.

provenance.reasoning: No observable pass/fail condition — 'feel seamless' cannot be verified or refuted.
provenance.source_quote: the experience should feel seamless to end users

findings.suggested_rewrite: Fewer than 2% of migrated users file a login-related ticket in the first 30 days.

provenance.reasoning: Names no artifact, no audience, and no condition under which it counts as done.

findings.suggested_rewrite: Publish an SSO runbook and an end-user FAQ; both linked from the login error page.

provenance.reasoning: A big-bang cutover with no rollback plan anywhere in the document. The spec's own subject makes the absence conspicuous: if Monday sign-in fails, there is no stated way back.
provenance.source_quote: All users will be cut over in a single weekend migration

findings.suggested_rewrite: State the rollback: legacy stack stays warm for N days, re-pointing DNS/auth config restores it within M minutes, and name the rollback decision owner.

provenance.reasoning: Centralizing all authentication with no stated security requirements: no session invalidation policy for the legacy stack, no penetration/security review gate, no availability target for the IdP that is now a single point of failure.
provenance.source_quote: The new IdP will handle all authentication for internal and customer-facing apps

findings.suggested_rewrite: Add an NFR block: IdP availability target, legacy session invalidation at cutover, and a security review sign-off before customer-facing apps move.

provenance.reasoning: The plan depends on IT provisioning a tenant, but no requirement, date, or agreement with IT is stated anywhere — the dependency is assumed, not declared.
provenance.source_quote: Once the Okta tenant is provisioned by IT

findings.suggested_rewrite: Add a dependency line: Okta tenant provisioned by IT by <date>, owner named, tracked as a predecessor to integration work.

provenance.reasoning: Assumes every user is on an app version that supports the new flow; nothing in the document requires a minimum version, a forced upgrade, or a fallback for old clients.
provenance.source_quote: Mobile clients will pick up the new flow automatically

findings.suggested_rewrite: State the minimum supported app version and the behavior for older clients, or add a forced-upgrade requirement before cutover.

provenance.reasoning: Cannot hold together with Requirements: 'Legacy login remains available for 90 days after cutover so stragglers can migrate.' The stack cannot be both decommissioned immediately and available for 90 days.
provenance.source_quote: The legacy auth stack will be decommissioned immediately after the cutover weekend

findings.suggested_rewrite: Pick one: keep legacy read-only for 90 days then decommission, or decommission immediately and delete the 90-day promise.

provenance.reasoning: Cannot hold together with Rollout: 'All users will be cut over in a single weekend migration.' A single-weekend cutover and a department-by-department Q4 rollout are different plans with different risk profiles.
provenance.source_quote: Departments will migrate one at a time through Q4

findings.suggested_rewrite: Choose the rollout shape and make the other section agree; the risk, comms, and rollback story all differ between the two.

provenance.reasoning: A team is not an accountable owner; when the runbook is late there is no named person to ask. This is the realistic version of unowned scope — it looks owned.
provenance.source_quote: The platform team will own the migration runbook

findings.suggested_rewrite: Name the individual: '<name> (platform) owns the migration runbook, reviewed by <name> before cutover.'

provenance.reasoning: Passive voice with no producer: nobody is accountable for the materials existing.
provenance.source_quote: Training materials will be produced before launch

findings.suggested_rewrite: '<name> delivers training materials by <date>; sign-off by department leads.'
